content: 1. Uribe-Sales F conducted an evaluation of a rapid diagnostic test to determine the prevalence of maternal syphilis in Bolivia. The findings were published in the Revista Médica de Chile in 2009, volume 137, issue 4, pages 515–521. 2. Terris-Prestholt F, Vickerman P, Torres-Rueda S, Santesso N, Sweeney S, Mallma P, and colleagues analyzed the cost-effectiveness of ten antenatal syphilis screening and treatment approaches in Peru, Tanzania, and Zambia. Their study was published in the International Journal of Gynaecology and Obstetrics in 2015, volume 130 (Supplement 1), pages S73–S80. 3. Hawkes SJ, Gomez GB, and Broutet N conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess whether early antenatal care improves pregnancy outcomes associated with syphilis. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2013, volume 8, article e56713. 4. Nnko S, Changalucha J, Mosha J, Bunga C, Wamoyi J, Peeling R, and Mabey D explored perceptions, attitudes, and the uptake of rapid syphilis testing services in antenatal clinics in North-Western Tanzania. Their study was published in Health Policy and Planning in 2016, volume 31, issue 5, pages 667–673. 5. The International Drug Price Indicator Guide (2014 edition, updated annually) provides cost-related data and was accessed on July 10, 2017. 6. Terris-Prestholt F, Vickerman P, Torres-Rueda S, Santesso N, Sweeney S, Mallma P, and colleagues also examined the cost-effectiveness of antenatal syphilis screening and treatment approaches in Peru, Tanzania, and Zambia, as published in the International Journal of Gynaecology and Obstetrics in 2015, volume 130 (Supplement 1), pages S73–S80. 7. Ansbro ÉM, Gill MM, Reynolds J, Shelley KD, Strasser S, Sripipatana T, and colleagues conducted a qualitative study on the introduction of syphilis point-of-care tests in Zambia, from pilot studies to national program implementation. They analyzed healthcare workers’ perspectives on testing, training, and quality assurance. The study was published in PLoS One in 2015, volume 10, issue 6, article e0127728. 8. Hawkes S, Matin N, Broutet N, and Low N performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions aimed at improving syphilis screening during pregnancy. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2011, volume 11, pages 684–691. 9. Hawkes SJ, Gomez GB, and Broutet N also reviewed the impact of early antenatal care on pregnancy outcomes related to syphilis, with their findings published in PLoS One in 2013, volume 8, article e56713. 10. Kleutsch L, Harvey SA, and Rennie W documented the challenges and progress in adopting rapid syphilis tests in Tanzania. This case study was published by the Center for Human Services in Bethesda, MD, in 2009. 11. Mabey DC, Sollis KA, Kelly HA, Benzaken AS, Bitarakwate E, Changalucha J, and colleagues highlighted the role of point-of-care tests in strengthening health systems and reducing neonatal mortality due to syphilis. Their work was published in PLoS Medicine in 2012, volume 9, issue 6, article e1001233. 12. Nnko S, Changalucha J, Mosha J, Bunga C, Wamoyi J, Peeling R, and Mabey D investigated the perceptions, attitudes, and uptake of rapid syphilis testing services in antenatal clinics in North-Western Tanzania. Their findings were published in Health Policy and Planning in 2016, volume 31, issue 5, pages 667–673. 13. Strasser S, Bitarakwate E, Gill M, Hoffman HJ, Musana O, Phiri A, and colleagues conducted a field study on the acceptability and feasibility of introducing rapid syphilis testing within programs aimed at preventing mother-to-child transmission of HIV in Uganda and Zambia. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012, volume 61, pages e40–e46. 14. Vickerman P, Peeling RW, Terris-Prestholt F, Changalucha J, Mabey D, Watson-Jones D, and Watts C modeled the cost-effectiveness of introducing rapid syphilis tests into antenatal syphilis screening programs in Mwanza, Tanzania. Their study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2006, volume 82 (Supplement 5), pages v38–v43.
